newsitem.title: SPAIN: China copper concs buying may change - Champagne.
newsitem.headline: China copper concs buying may change - Champagne.

text.p: The whole process whereby China buys copper concentrates from the west may change in coming years, and purchasing could shift back to the centre, John Champagne, Chief Operating Officer at Global Minerals and Metals Corp, said on Wednesday.

Chinese demand for copper concentrates from the west was expected to amount to one million tonnes in the future, which would be difficult to maintain from the spot trader market, Champagne said at Metal Bulletin's International Copper Conference.
"At the moment it (buying) is done on a decentralised basis, but as imports grow larger it will be difficult to manage," Champagne said.
There could be a re-centralisation process and a move towards long-term deals with producers, rather than spot business concluded with traders, he said.
If that did occur, it would be a slow and difficult process because there were many hurdles to overcome.
For instance, many traders were reluctant to sell copper concentrates to China due to the difficulty in receiving credits for gold by-products.
This was because Chinese regulations required the gold by-product to be sold domestically, and a 10 percent discount to the international bullion price.
"Something has to be done to change this and make China more competitive when bidding for concentrates with a high gold content," Champagne said.

Meanwhile, China was expected to be the dominant force in a booming Asian region. This region was expected to account for 50 percent of world copper consumption in 10 years time compared with two-thirds at present, Champagne said.
"There is more intensity of use, as people's improving lifestyles demand more copper," he said.
